catalyst_text: Announced positive updated results in advanced systemic mastocytosis
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated results from the registration-directed APEX study in advanced systemic mastocytosis were reported. The data showed a 65% ORR by mIWG-MRT-ECNM and 81% ORR by PPR, with strong reductions in mast cell burden and favorable tolerability. These findings underscore robust clinical activity in a high-need population.
catalyst_text_evidence: On 2026-06-12, Cogent Biosciences, Inc. ... today announced detailed and updated clinical results from the registration-directed APEX clinical trial of bezuclastinib in patients with advanced systemic mastocytosis (AdvSM) demonstrating clinically meaningful results as measured by consensus criteria used to assess patient response. As of the updated data cutoff of 2026-03-31 in Part 2 of the APEX trial, 81 AdvSM patients were treated with 150 mg of bezuclastinib, including 57 patients with SM-AHN, 11 patients with ASM and 13 patients with MCL. The primary endpoint of response per mIWG-MRT-ECNM was assessed on 68 evaluable patients and showed 65% ORR (CR+CRh+PR+CI), including 57% of patients who achieved CR, CRh or PR as best response. Key secondary endpoint of response per pure pathological response (PPR) criteria was assessed on 81 patients which showed an 81% ORR (CR+CRh+PR). Bezuclastinib demonstrated a powerful effect on mast cell burden with 91% of patients achieving ≥50% reduction in variant allele frequency and 89% of patients achieving ≥50% reduction in bone marrow mast cells or clearance of aggregates.

drug_indication: Imatinib-resistant or intolerant Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors (GIST)
catalyst_text: Cogent reported positive topline Phase 3 PEAK results for bezuclastinib plus sunitinib in imatinib-resistant or intolerant GIST, meeting the PFS primary endpoint (mPFS 16.5 vs 9.2 months vs sunitinib). The company plans to present full PEAK results at a scientific conference in the first half of 2026 and is on track to submit an NDA in the first half of 2026.

drug_indication: First-line Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors with KIT exon 9 mutations
catalyst_text: Initiated first line exon nine GIST extension cohort
detailed_catalyst_text: A single-arm, 40-patient extension cohort of the PEAK trial was initiated to evaluate the combination in first-line GIST patients with KIT exon 9 mutations who have received limited or no imatinib. The cohort will prospectively assess objective response rate and progression-free survival in this molecularly defined population. This initiation expands development into the first-line setting for exon 9 patients.
catalyst_text_evidence: Cogent announces initiation of new clinical trial of bezuclastinib combination in 1L GIST patients. Cogent also announced today the initiation of a single-arm, 40 patient extension cohort of the PEAK trial investigating the safety and efficacy of the bezuclastinib combination in first-line GIST patients with KIT exon 9 primary mutations who have received limited or no imatinib treatment. This cohort is designed to prospectively measure ORR and PFS in this patient population. As reported in November 2025, PEAK is a global, randomized Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating bezuclastinib in combination with sunitinib vs. sunitinib monotherapy in patients with imatinib-resistant or intolerant GIST.

catalyst_text: Priority review granted positive results PDUFA Nov 30
detailed_catalyst_text: The NDA for the combination in patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumors previously treated with imatinib was accepted and granted Priority Review, with a PDUFA date set for November 30, 2026. The company also reported detailed, positive Phase 3 PEAK primary analysis results showing a significant progression-free survival benefit versus sunitinib alone. This supports the regulatory review with robust efficacy and tolerability data in the post-imatinib setting.
catalyst_text_evidence: Priority Review granted following FDA acceptance of NDA for bezuclastinib combination in GIST patients who previously received imatinib; PDUFA date scheduled for 2026-11-30. Cogent Biosciences, Inc. today announced detailed clinical data from the primary analysis of the PEAK Phase 3 trial of bezuclastinib in combination with sunitinib in patients with Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors (GIST) who have received prior treatment with imatinib. As of the cutoff date, 2025-09-30, the bezuclastinib combination demonstrated a substantial and highly statistically significant clinical benefit on the primary endpoint of PFS, reducing risk of disease progression or death compared to the current standard of care by 50% (hazard ratio of 0.50, 95% CI: 0.39 – 0.65). mPFS, as assessed by blinded independent central review, was 16.5 months for the bezuclastinib combination vs. 9.2 months for sunitinib monotherapy.

catalyst_text: NDA accepted with priority review PDUFA November 2026
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA accepted the NDA for a combination regimen to treat Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors after prior imatinib and granted Priority Review, assigning a PDUFA action date of 2026-11-30. The agency also indicated no advisory committee is planned and no potential review issues have been identified. This acceptance with priority review underscores an expedited evaluation for a population with limited options.
catalyst_text_evidence: Cogent Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:COGT), a biotechnology company focused on developing precision therapies for genetically defined diseases, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted its New Drug Application (NDA) for bezuclastinib in combination with sunitinib for patients with Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors (GIST) who have received prior treatment with imatinib. The FDA has granted the application Priority Review and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of 2026-11-30. In addition, the FDA communicated that at this time, there is no plan to hold an advisory committee, nor have they identified any potential review issues.

catalyst_text: Submitted NDA under RTOR for GIST treatment
detailed_catalyst_text: A New Drug Application for bezuclastinib in combination with sunitinib was submitted under the Real-Time Oncology Review program in March 2026 for patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors previously treated with imatinib. This filing initiates formal regulatory review and may expedite assessment of the therapy for this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Top line results were reported in November 2025, and the New Drug Application was submitted under the Real-Time Oncology Review (RTOR) program in March 2026.

catalyst_text: NDA submitted under RTOR supported by positive data
detailed_catalyst_text: A U.S. NDA was completed for use in Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors previously treated with imatinib and submitted under the FDA Real-Time Oncology Review program. The filing is supported by pivotal Phase 3 PEAK results showing a 50% reduction in risk of progression or death and longer median PFS versus sunitinib in second-line patients.
catalyst_text_evidence: Cogent Biosciences, Inc. ... today announced the completion of the submission of its New Drug Application (NDA) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for bezuclastinib in patients with Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors (GIST) who have received prior treatment with imatinib. Based on the positive results from the PEAK trial, the bezuclastinib NDA was submitted under the FDA's Real-Time Oncology Review (RTOR) program, which is intended to enable a more streamlined review process. As disclosed in the top-line results, the bezuclastinib combination demonstrated a substantial and highly statistically significant clinical benefit on the primary endpoint of progression free survival (PFS), reducing risk of disease progression or death compared to the current standard of care by 50% (hazard ratio of 0.50, 95% CI: 0.39 – 0.65). mPFS, as assessed by blinded independent central review, was 16.5 months for the bezuclastinib combination vs. 9.2 months for sunitinib monotherapy.

catalyst_text: NDA accepted with PDUFA date December 30 2026
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA accepted the NDA for bezuclastinib to treat patients with non-advanced systemic mastocytosis and assigned a PDUFA target action date of December 30, 2026. The agency indicated no plan for an advisory committee and noted no potential review issues, suggesting a straightforward review process.
catalyst_text_evidence: Cogent Biosciences, Inc. ... today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted its New Drug Application (NDA) for bezuclastinib in patients with NonAdvanced Systemic Mastocytosis (NonAdvSM) and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of 2026-12-30. In addition, the FDA communicated that at this time, there is no plan to hold an advisory committee, nor have they identified any potential review issues.

catalyst_text: Presented positive pivotal trial results at AAAAI meeting
detailed_catalyst_text: Additional clinical results from the pivotal SUMMIT trial in Non-Advanced Systemic Mastocytosis were presented at the AAAAI Annual Meeting, showing statistically significant symptom improvements that deepened through 48 weeks along with high rates of serum tryptase reduction and normalization. The data also showed improvements in bone mineral density and reductions in supportive care use, supporting a potential disease-modifying effect and favorable tolerability in this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Cogent Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:COGT)... today announced additional clinical results from the pivotal SUMMIT trial with bezuclastinib in patients with NonAdvanced Systemic Mastocytosis (NonAdvSM) at the American Academy of Allergy Asthma & Immunology (AAAAI) Annual Meeting. As previously reported, bezuclastinib demonstrated clinically meaningful and highly statistically significant improvements across the primary and all key secondary endpoints. New results highlight the deepening of clinical benefit over longer treatment duration, the benefit of bezuclastinib in populations with high unmet need, and bezuclastinib's impact on bone mineral density as additional evidence of disease modification. Patients on bezuclastinib reported a -32.0 point mean change in TSS, representing a 56% relative improvement in TSS from baseline. 86% of patients achieved a clinically meaningful threshold of 30% improvement in symptoms. 99% of patients had at least 50% reduction in serum tryptase, with 83.3% of patients achieving normalization.

catalyst_text: Received Breakthrough Therapy Designation and RTOR acceptance
detailed_catalyst_text: FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation for the combination therapy in GIST patients previously treated with imatinib, based on substantial clinical benefit observed in the PEAK study. The agency also agreed to accept the NDA under the Real-Time Oncology Review program, allowing pre-submission review of components to expedite evaluation. These regulatory actions can accelerate review timelines and reflect strong supporting data.
catalyst_text_evidence: Cogent Biosciences, Inc. today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation (BTD) for bezuclastinib in combination with sunitinib for patients with Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors (GIST) who have received prior treatment with imatinib. Earlier this month, the FDA agreed to accept Cogent's NDA under the FDA's Real-Time Oncology Review (RTOR) program which allows an applicant to pre-submit components of its NDA to allow the FDA to review clinical trial data before the complete filing is submitted and aims to provide a more efficient review process to ensure safe and effective treatments are available to patients as early as possible.

catalyst_text: FDA RTOR acceptance announced and data highly positive
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA agreed to accept an NDA under the Real-Time Oncology Review program for a combination therapy in GIST patients previously treated with imatinib. Previously reported PEAK trial results showed a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival and a higher response rate versus sunitinib alone. This regulatory step, supported by strong efficacy data, advances the therapy toward potential approval.
catalyst_text_evidence: Cogent Biosciences, Inc. … announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has agreed to accept its New Drug Application (NDA) for bezuclastinib in combination with sunitinib for patients with Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors (GIST) who have received prior treatment with imatinib under the Real-Time Oncology Review (RTOR) program. mPFS, as assessed by blinded independent central review, was 16.5 months for the bezuclastinib combination vs. 9.2 months for sunitinib monotherapy. Additionally, the bezuclastinib combination demonstrated an unprecedented overall response rate (ORR) in imatinib-resistant patients, with 46% of patients treated with the bezuclastinib combination achieving an objective response compared to 26% of patients treated with sunitinib.

catalyst_text: Announced positive topline results in pivotal AdvSM study
detailed_catalyst_text: Reported positive top-line data from the registration-directed APEX Part 2 trial in advanced systemic mastocytosis, including a 57% ORR by mIWG criteria and 80% by PPR criteria with strong biomarker reductions. Safety was favorable with no discontinuations due to treatment-related adverse events and limited dose reductions. These pivotal results are clinically meaningful for this patient population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Cogent Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:COGT) today announced positive top-line results from the registration-directed APEX Part 2 clinical trial of bezuclastinib in patients with advanced systemic mastocytosis (AdvSM) demonstrating clinically meaningful results as measured by consensus criteria used to assess patient response. Primary endpoint: 57% ORR (CR+CRh+PR+CI) per mIWG-MRT-ECNM (mIWG) criteria. Key secondary endpoint: 80% ORR (CR+CRh+PR) per pure pathological response (PPR) criteria. Bezuclastinib was very well tolerated with only 14.8% of patients requiring dose reduction and no patients requiring discontinuation due to treatment related adverse events.

catalyst_text: Announced positive registrational results in nonadvanced systemic mastocytosis
detailed_catalyst_text: Announced complete results from the registration-directed Part 2 of the SUMMIT randomized study in nonadvanced systemic mastocytosis. The trial met the primary and key secondary endpoints with highly statistically significant improvements in symptoms and objective disease markers, with a favorable safety profile. Results also showed a significant correlation between reductions in disease pathology and improvements in patient-reported symptom severity.
catalyst_text_evidence: Cogent Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:COGT) today announced complete results from the registration-directed Part 2 of the SUMMIT clinical trial of bezuclastinib in patients with nonadvanced systemic mastocytosis (NonAdvSM). As previously reported, bezuclastinib demonstrated clinically meaningful and highly statistically significant improvements across the primary and all key secondary endpoints. New results further highlight the benefit of bezuclastinib on patient-reported symptoms and objective measures of mast cell burden and demonstrate significant correlation between improvement in disease pathology and patient-reported symptom severity. Bezuclastinib delivered clinically meaningful and statistically significant symptomatic improvement. At week 24, 87.4% of patients achieved ≥50% reduction in serum tryptase levels, 75.6% of patients demonstrated ≥50% reduction in bone marrow mast cells or clearance of aggregates and 85.7% of patients achieved ≥50% reduction in KIT D816V variant allele frequency or undetectable, each of which was statistically significant when compared to placebo. As previously reported on 2025-07-07, the majority of treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs) (98.3% in bezuclastinib arm vs. 88.3% in placebo arm) were of low grade.

catalyst_text: Cogent plans to announce top-line results from the pivotal, registration-directed APEX trial in Advanced Systemic Mastocytosis in December 2025. APEX is a global, open-label study. The readout will provide the first pivotal dataset for bezuclastinib in AdvSM. Results are intended to inform potential regulatory next steps.

Cogent plans to submit its first NDA for bezuclastinib in NonAdvSM by the end of 2025 and present multiple bezuclastinib data sets at the 2025 ASH Annual Meeting, including two oral presentations from the pivotal SUMMIT trial. These activities support the planned NDA and program visibility.
